rationale: Record the newterm receipt and extend the account to the ordinary re-synchronization producer. Receipt 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 (all four tests passed) showed that a follower which merely re-promised in a new term created by an ordinary leader change - with no reconnected() call - ended at accepted 7 over its six indices of content, its reconfiguration endpoint flipped to false, its StopSign index read returned None and its decided-log read from 0 returned nothing (event 11), while the new leader and the node that received no message stayed at 6/6 (events 9, 10) and the pre-change baseline held (events 6-8). The trigger is therefore the resume point covering the StopSign, not the reconnection API. The indexed knowledge is re-conditioned on all three receipts, the interpretation covers the three runs separately with their controls, the snapshot/leader half of the open gap is answered again (one half witnessed for followers, the leader-side instance still unexecuted), and a successor experiment is submitted that unblocks the cut-off node and lets it take the lead, so a leader whose own decided index is the followers' resume point is sampled.

investigations.discriminator: Whether a leader whose own decided index becomes the resume point ends up inflated in its own accepted index (targeted by the successor's staleleader stage), and whether a snapshot-enabled configuration reproduces or avoids the inflation.

knowledge.statement: InternalStorage::sync_log sets accepted_idx = LogSync.sync_idx + LogSync.suffix.len() and, when LogSync.stopsign is Some, adds one further index for that StopSign before returning; it does not subtract the LogSync's prefix, so when sync_idx already addresses the StopSign's own index the replica's accepted index ends up one larger than the entries it holds. SequencePaxos::create_log_sync does not adjust sync_idx for a StopSign already present on the sender: it uses its caller's common_prefix_idx unchanged and attaches the sender's stored StopSign.
knowledge.conditions: Reached when a follower applies an AcceptSync whose LogSync carries stopsign = Some; the accounting is unconditional with respect to whether the resumed prefix already contained a StopSign. Exercised in three receipts: two reconnected followers ended at accepted 7 over six indices of content (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 22, 23), one reconnected follower did the same (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35), and a follower that merely re-promised in a new term after an ordinary leader change did the same with no reconnected() call (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11), while the pre-change samples and the no-reconnect control stayed at 6/6 with a six-element decided read (events 6-8, 9, 10 and 19-21, 9-11).

knowledge.statement: On a replica that already holds the accepted StopSign, applying an AcceptSync whose LogSync carries that StopSign leaves the stored log unchanged while the reported accepted index rises by one; the replica's read of the StopSign's previous index (5) then returns None, its read of index 6 returns the StopSign, and read_decided_suffix(0) returns a decided log that omits the five entries: one element (the StopSign) when the replica's decided index has been pushed past that index, and an empty list when its decided index still stops there.
knowledge.conditions: Three-node cluster, five decided entries plus a StopSign, no snapshots (NoSnapshot), default batch size, the re-synchronized replica having already accepted the StopSign. Both decided-index positions and both producers were observed: two followers re-synchronized after reconnected() calls (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 22, 23 with a one-element read; 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 events 22, 23), one follower re-synchronized after reconnected() (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35 with an empty read and decided index 6), and one follower re-promised in a new term created by an ordinary leader change with no reconnected() call (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11: accepted 7, decided 6, empty decided read, endpoint false).

knowledge.statement: The inflated accepted index follows from the resume point being compared against the index the StopSign occupies in the receiving replica's accounting: sync_log computes accepted_idx = LogSync.sync_idx + LogSync.suffix.len() and adds one for a carried StopSign, while the StopSign occupies the index accepted_idx - 1 and the sender attaches it without shifting sync_idx. The condition is therefore sync_idx + suffix.len() >= the StopSign's index, and it does not depend on the snapshot option: the no-snapshot branch passes the caller's common_prefix_idx unchanged (for a re-promising follower that is its own accepted index, which already counts the StopSign), whereas the snapshot branch passes the compacted index returned by create_diff_snapshot, which is derived from get_decided_idx_without_stopsign and therefore excludes the StopSign.
knowledge.conditions: Holds for any LogSync whose stopsign is Some; the snapshot branch is only entered when T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true and the sender's decided index exceeds common_prefix_idx. Three observed producer instances of the condition: a follower re-synchronized after reconnected() at the same ballot (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8, 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63) and a follower re-presenting its accepted index when it re-promises in a new term after an ordinary leader change (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11). A further sourced instance not yet executed: a candidate leader whose own decided index becomes common_prefix_idx in the follower's Promise, which would inflate the leader's own accepted index; and no snapshot-enabled run has been executed.

knowledge.statement: A leader in the accept phase accepts a decision at the accepted index reported by any matching-ballot Accepted message: it records that index for the sender, and if the index exceeds its own decided index and a write quorum of recorded accepted indexes covers it, it sets its decided index to exactly that reported index, without comparing it against the length of its own log or against its own accepted index.
knowledge.conditions: Leader role in Phase::Accept with a matching ballot; the recorded accepted indexes include the leader's own slot as it was last written by its own accept handling. Observed: with two inflated reports the leader reported decided index 7 while holding six indices and its own accepted index stayed 6 (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 event 24; reproduced in 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 24), while a single inflated report left the leader at 6/6 (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37) and, in the newterm case, one inflated follower plus a node that received nothing also left the new leader at 6/6 (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9).

interpretations.rationale: Three receipts now support one index-space confusion with two consequences, and the third shows the trigger is not the reconnected() call. (1) A replica that already accepted the configuration's StopSign and is handed a resume point that already covers it ends with accepted index one past its content: this happened for a follower re-synchronized after reconnected() (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35) and, with no reconnected() call at all, for a follower that merely re-promised in a new term after an ordinary leader change (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11: accepted 7, decided 6, is_reconfigured false, read(5) none, read(6) stop_sign, decided-log read from 0 empty), while the new leader and the cut-off node stayed at 6/6 (events 9, 10) and the pre-change baseline held for all three (events 6-8). (2) When a write quorum of such inflated reports reaches one leader, that leader decides the reported index although it holds fewer indices: with both followers re-synchronized the leader reported decided 7 with accepted 6 (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 and 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 24), after which it no longer reported the reconfiguration as decided and its decided log read returned None; with only one inflated reporter no quorum was reached and the leader stayed consistent (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 events 36, 37; 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9). The mechanism is the same in all three runs: create_log_sync passes a resume point expressed in the accepted-count space (which counts the StopSign as an index) while sync_log adds the carried StopSign again for a receiver whose content already includes it (send_accsync's first and second branches, leader.rs 150-191; follower Promise, follower.rs 13-51; accounting, internal_storage.rs 313-360, 503-512). The remaining sourced instance of the same condition is a candidate leader whose own decided index becomes the resume point; the successor experiment submitted here adds a third stage in which the previously cut-off node takes the lead so its own sync is exercised.
counterevidence: The no-reconnect control kept every endpoint consistent (accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, six-element decided read: 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11), and in the newterm case the new leader and the node that received nothing stayed consistent (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 events 9, 10), so the deviation follows the re-synchronization of a replica whose resume point covers the StopSign rather than the reconfiguration or the harness.

The inflated accepted index is what the replica reports to the leader; the leader-side phantom decision additionally needs a write quorum of inflated reporters in one term (two of three nodes), which one inflated follower does not provide (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9; 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37).

The documented reconfiguration flow (agent-source/docs/omnipaxos/reconfiguration.md 25-34) expects a new instance once a node observes LogEntry::StopSign(ss, true), which narrows the window in which a user reads the old instance, but the leader never observes the decision after the corruption and the followers keep reporting it while their decided log silently loses the entries.
The leader's phantom decision is inferred from its reported state (decided 7 with accepted 6 and six indices of content) plus the inflated reports; the internal accepted-index vector was not sampled.
limitations: No snapshot-enabled execution has been run; the sourced applicability fact says the snapshot branch is not entered when the resume point equals the sender's decided index and derives sync_idx without the StopSign when it is entered, so the defect is not specific to NoSnapshot entries, but that branch was not exercised.

Loss-triggered and timer-triggered re-synchronization were not exercised: messages were delivered in FIFO order without loss and no tick() timers ran, so the observed producers are explicit reconnected() calls and a plain leader change with one node cut off.

The consequence is bounded by the sealed configuration: after the StopSign is accepted no further entries can be accepted, so the phantom decided index carries no value and no value is mis-assigned; the demonstrated effects are the corrupted index accounting, the unreadable or blank decided log and the lost reconfiguration endpoint rather than divergent values.

All three nodes used in-memory storage; persistence across a restart and other storages' behaviour on out-of-range reads (a storage-implementer responsibility per the Storage trait) were not exercised.

Only three-node clusters were exercised; larger clusters, repeated leader changes around the re-synchronization and a leader's own inflation through a follower's log_sync remain untested (the successor experiment targets the last of these).

e40cd046de9e4f37b5761260b8dc599e-gap-2.explanation: One half is now witnessed and one half remains open. On the snapshot half: in the observed configuration the sender's decided index equals the resume point, so create_log_sync does not take the snapshot branch even with T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() true (mod.rs 405-432), and when that branch is entered it sets sync_idx to the compacted index derived from get_decided_idx_without_stopsign (internal_storage.rs 385-412, 469-474), which excludes the StopSign; so the inflation is not specific to NoSnapshot entries, but no snapshot-enabled run has been executed. On the leader half: the path is sourced (a candidate whose own promise is not the maximum syncs from a follower whose Promise carries create_log_sync(prep.decided_idx, prep.decided_idx), so the candidate's decided index becomes sync_idx and the same +1 applies: follower.rs 13-51, leader.rs 257-285), and the successor submitted with this update adds a third stage in which the previously cut-off node takes the lead so its own accepted index is sampled; no execution has yet shown a leader inflated in its own accepted index.

interpretations.joint_history: Three successive invocations of the same harness lineage, read separately and never combined: 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 ran experiment 27bf7fc0875c4342966bd3dc15df80ec-experiment (resync, control), 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 ran 3ed5ddd94bce4e94a2dc5b7bb417c18a-experiment (same prefix and cases plus single-follower resync and a read of index 6), and 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 ran 3641dc6df2ae4993b82175d7b24cb702-experiment (same cases plus newterm). Same three-node setup, same public endpoints, same prefix; each successor reproduces the earlier witnesses (resync at events 22-24) and adds the new case.

knowledge.assertion: sync_log double-counts the StopSign when the resumed prefix already covers it
a re-synchronized replica's decided log read loses the entries
the condition is the resume point covering the StopSign's index
the leader decides the reported accepted index without bounding it to its own log

experiment.revision_reason: Adds a third stage to the newterm case: the previously cut-off node is unblocked and takes the lead, so a leader whose own decided index is the followers' resume point is sampled for inflation of its own accepted index.

scope.description: Five cases in one execution over three real OmniPaxos instances in one process with MemoryStorage and a deterministic FIFO in-process network: resync, single, control, newterm (with the added STALELEADER stage). In newterm node 2 is cut off while node 1 leads in a new term; then node 2 is unblocked and takes the lead itself, so its prepare collects promises whose log_sync carries the StopSign. Public API only; each lifecycle stage emits its own CA_EVENT name.
assumptions: Entry type Value has Snapshot = NoSnapshot, so create_log_sync takes its no-snapshot branch.
ClusterConfig { configuration_id: 1, nodes: [1,2,3], flexible_quorum: None } (majority 2) and default ServerConfig (batch_size 1).
Leadership is obtained with try_become_leader(); node 2's promise is still the original leader's ballot, so its new ballot outranks node 1's current ballot.
Cutting off node 2 means dropping messages addressed to it; unblocking restores ordinary FIFO delivery.
excluded: Snapshots, trimming, compaction and batching are not exercised.
No crate or package test suite is executed; only the generated test file.

experiment.prefix: Same prefix and cases as the fixed 3641dc6df2ae4993b82175d7b24cb702-experiment (node 3 leads, five entries decided, StopSign proposed and decided, then resync/single/control/newterm stages with samples of get_accepted_idx, get_decided_idx, is_reconfigured, read(5), read(6), read_decided_suffix(0)). The newterm case now continues after NEWTERM_AFTER: node 2 is unblocked and calls try_become_leader(), the queue is drained to quiet, and all three nodes are sampled as STALELEADER_AFTER.

comparisons.description: Baseline before the leader change: the StopSign is reported at its own index 5 by every replica.
Baseline before the leader change: every replica's decided log read from index 0 has six elements.
Baseline before the leader change: every replica reports the reconfiguration as decided.
Reproduction: a follower that merely re-promised in a new term still reports at most the six indices it holds.
Reproduction: that follower still reports the reconfiguration as decided.
The new leader's decided log read stays intact after the leader change.
The cut-off node's decided log read stays intact while it receives nothing.
A leader that syncs from followers still holds only the six indices of content, so its own accepted index stays 6.
That leader still reports the StopSign at its own index 5.
That leader's decided log read from index 0 still has six elements.
That leader still reports six decided indices rather than a decided index past its content.

semantic_changes: The newterm case gains a third stage that unblocks node 2 and lets it take the lead; the other cases and the compared fields are unchanged.
